description: The root actor, held by the orchestrator thread. Takes requests, keeps 2-4 items in flight within budget, and keeps the person's inbox. The orchestrator is the session that sent ORCHESTRATOR_STARTED last; items take its id from here. It also opens the day's stand-in audit (AUDIT_PICKED), once per day, as a child audit actor (spec audit). It holds the person's grant to the stand-in (context.grant, spec grant): GRANT_ASKED from a session opens a checklist card (a child grant actor, one open at a time: a new ask withdraws the unanswered one), and only the person sets or replaces the grant, by one of two sources for the same PERSON_GRANTED {picks}: a tap on that card, reported up as GRANT_GIVEN, or a chat message of theirs, named by its message id (source message:<cmsg id>) and sent to the harness itself, whose picks the relaying session reads from the person's words ("stop asking" is every kind and one-way, with no end time). harness verify-taps lists both, so another session can check each against its card or message. Every decision the stand-in makes under a grant reports itself (DECIDED_UNDER_GRANT), and the harness keeps it in context.granted, one compact row each ({address, item, decisionClass, door, choice, confidence, reason, card, at}), so mission control and the daily audit list every one with its reason for the person to reverse. A decision waiting on the person (in the inbox) whose class and door the live grant covers at the event's own time can be sent back to the stand-in for a fresh answer: REASK_UNDER_GRANT {decision: <decision id>} from the orchestrator takes it out of the inbox and passes it to the decision through its item, so a decision stuck before a grant, or before the grant decided whatever the confidence, moves on without a tap.

person.description: The person: acts only by a tap on a card the machine asked for, or, for a grant alone, by a chat message of theirs named by its message id, and holds no role.

session.description: A Claude Code session (a thread): id CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID, which the CLI takes from the platform. It never contains '/'.

agent.description: A subagent of a session: id <session_id>/<agent_id>, the session's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and the agent_id of the hook input, so it names both; type is its agent_type. The plugin's PreToolUse hook hands it to every harness call a subagent runs (HARNESS_AGENT=<agent_id>:<agent_type>) and the CLI records it as this actor; its SubagentStart hook files a record that harness verify-actors checks it against, its window starting at the earliest start recorded for it (that record, the bind's start-<agent_id> call, or the WORKER_STARTED row in the same store that names it by id, sent by its parent session) and ending at its session's last filed turn. A resume (SendMessage to an agent that ran) fires SubagentStart again: the record keeps its first start and bind, and adds the resume's time. Two subagents of one session are two actors, and neither is the session.

github.description: GitHub: only through harness from-github, after its REST API agrees.

timer.description: The harness's own clock (tick, digest, canary).

sources.tap: The person's tap on a card the machine asked for: ref is the card's message id, which the ack of its card effect recorded. Relayed by a session (relayedBy).
sources.message: The person's chat message: ref is its message id (cmsg_...). Taken only for a grant (PERSON_GRANTED to the harness) and relayed by a session (relayedBy); harness verify-taps lists it so another session reads the message (read_messages_by_id) and checks the grant matches its words.
sources.github-wake: A GitHub wake: only through harness from-github, after its REST API agrees; ref is the fact read.
sources.cli: The harness CLI, run by a session or a subagent: ref names the command.
sources.timer: The harness's own clock: ref is the time.

meta.roles: Actors marked roles (session and agent) are recorded in an item's roles and compared there by the whole actor, kind and id: the id patterns are disjoint, so the recorded id names one actor. An event whose actor is not one of these kinds, or whose id does not match its kind's pattern, is refused before any machine sees it.

agentEvents.description: An agent actor (harness meta.actors) sends only the events its role on the addressed item allows, and nothing else, to any actor: its role is the role of a spawn of that item it is bound to (spec workItem, Workers: WORKER_SPAWNED, then WORKER_STARTED). The item is the one the event is addressed to, item:<id> or one of its decisions item:<id>/<decision>. An agent bound to no spawn of that item, an agent sending to the harness root, and an event its role does not list are refused before any machine sees the event. Sessions, the person, GitHub and timers are not agents and are not judged here.

invariants.envelope: runtime.apply refuses an event without an actor of a kind in meta.actors (its id of that form) and a source of a kind in meta.sources, or one carrying "person", before any machine sees it; under CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID a tap or a message also names the session that relayed it (relayedBy).
invariants.prBinding: runtime.apply refuses an event naming a PR bound to another item, or naming another PR than its item is bound to: one PR binds to one item, once (src/pr-binding.js).
invariants.tapOnly: runtime.apply refuses an event from a person, a tap or a message unless a machine takes it from the person (the events guarded by unattested with actor person: each binds a tap to its card, or, PERSON_GRANTED to the harness, names the message).
invariants.setsHarnessAgent: The plugin's PreToolUse hook denies a Bash command that sets, exports, clears or passes HARNESS_AGENT or HARNESS_CALL itself: only the hook sets them.
invariants.hookSawCall: The plugin's PreToolUse hook records a Bash call before it runs (session, agent_id, tool_use_id, command hash, time, the sha256 of a fresh random key, and whether the hook's own environment has HARNESS_ENFORCE=1) and stamps the command with HARNESS_CALL=<tool_use_id>:<key>; under HARNESS_ENFORCE=1 it records every Bash call, else those that name harness. The CLI believes a call's actor only when that record exists, the key hashes to the record's, and the record names that session and agent: an id the caller wrote itself, or another call's id, is refused. A recorded call made under HARNESS_ENFORCE=1 marks its store enforced (enforced.json in the store, naming the Library that holds the records), and an enforced store takes a write only from a recorded call, whatever the caller's own environment holds; the CLI never reads HARNESS_ENFORCE.
invariants.roleLine: The spawn gate reads a brief's role from one line 'Harness-Role: <role> item:<id>' naming an item in the store; under HARNESS_ENFORCE=1 a brief with a malformed or repeated role line, or a harness:builder or harness:verifier spawn without one, is denied.
invariants.oneUnboundSpawn: runtime.apply refuses WORKER_SPAWNED while the sending session has another spawn of the same agent type, on any item, that is unbound, not closed and inside the bind window (workItem noSpawnToBind withinMs), and the spawn gate denies the Agent call naming this rule. The SubagentStart hook's input names the agent and its type but not the Agent call it came from, so the hook binds a new agent to the one spawn of its type that waits; a machine guard sees only its own item, and this rule spans items. Its refusal names the waiting spawn: wait for its agent to start (WORKER_STARTED), or close it (SPAWN_CLOSED) if it never will.
invariants.storeReachable: Under HARNESS_ENFORCE=1 the spawn and merge gates deny a call they must judge when the store or the harness CLI cannot be read.
invariants.mergeBound: Under HARNESS_ENFORCE=1 the merge gate, which judges the GitHub MCP merge tool (mcp__github__merge_pull_request) and reads no Bash command, denies a merge of a PR it cannot name, or one bound to no item.
invariants.pinnedHead: Under HARNESS_ENFORCE=1 the merge gate denies a merge call that does not pin the head sha (expectedHeadSha).
invariants.reviewOnHead: Under HARNESS_ENFORCE=1 the merge gate denies a merge unless the PR carries the item's PASS verdict as a review on the pinned head sha (commit_id), read from GitHub's REST API: the review id the store holds, in state COMMENTED, its body the stored verdict text verbatim or that text followed by exactly meta.reviewFooter (the body trimmed). harness doctor audits every PR that GitHub's REST API says landed on main at or after the store's first event (an older landing is outside what the store can judge), in each repository the store names (its bound PRs' and its requests' issues'), bound to an item or not, and each landed PR bound to an item: a landing whose head has no verifier PASS in the store, or no review carrying it by the same comparison, is a problem, so a landing by any route the gate does not see is found after the fact. The exception is a landing an OUT_OF_BAND row of the history records (history.schema.json: the row's pr is the PR, and its sha, when it names one, is the head that landed): doctor lists that landing out of band, with who ordered it and the gates it skipped, and does not count it as a problem. A landing no row records is still a problem.
invariants.writerNotOlder: runtime.apply refuses an event from a release older than the one that last wrote the store (state.json writtenBy; a store from before the field: its last log row's harness): an older plugin version, or none, is refused, and at the same version a writer on another commit is refused unless the store's commit is an ancestor of its own (in the writer's git checkout). A store that records no version takes any writer; one whose version is not x.y.z takes none. The refusal names both releases (version@commit): older code would decide today's events by yesterday's rules. Replay applies facts and does not check the writer.
invariants.personNotFromAgent: The CLI refuses --actor person in a subagent's call (HARNESS_AGENT): a subagent records only as itself, so it cannot relay the person's tap or message.
invariants.oneWriter: store.withLock refuses a writer ("another writer holds") while another holds the store's lock, and every write to a store's logs or state.json holds it: apply, init, ack and repair, which rewrites a log in place. A lock older than 60s is stale and the next writer removes it, but only the writer that first claims that lock (an exclusive file named after its inode and time): a writer that found it stale after another took the lock again is refused. A claim older than 60s is stale too (its claimant crashed before removing the lock), and the next writer takes it over the same way: only the writer that first claims that claim. The writer that wins a claim removes the lock only while it is still the lock it found (same inode and time), so a writer that stalled between finding the lock stale and claiming it, while another broke it and took the lock again, is refused.

reviewFooter.description: The attribution footer this host's GitHub proxy appends to every comment and review a session posts, so a verdict review GitHub holds is the stored verdict text followed by it. The merge gate (reviewOnHead) and doctor's audit tolerate exactly this footer and nothing else: any other change to the body, text after the footer included, still fails the comparison that stops a forged or edited review from passing.

store.description: The layout of a store's state.json. Every write records the spec's schemaVersion beside the snapshot, and the release that wrote it (writtenBy: the plugin's version and the git commit; writerNotOlder); a state.json without schemaVersion was written before the field and has layout absentMeans. A page declares the range it reads (pages/<page>/needs.json, reads.schemaVersion) and, on a store outside it, shows a red banner naming the mismatch and no data. Raise it when a change moves or renames anything a page reads.
store.closes: A machine closes its own pending effects: an action may ask the runtime to close the pending effects of one subject by name (closeEffects). workItem's withdrawDecision asks for it, with its params closes, when it stops a decision that has not decided: the item leaves the gate on any event but that decision's own DECISION_MADE (a decided decision's ask is acked by its answer). runtime.apply writes an ack for each such effect still pending, outcome withdrawn, its note naming the subject and the event that withdrew it, in the same write as the event; it queues no effect for it. Nothing else closes an effect but the host's ack.
store.facts: A logged event is a fact: it was admitted once, by the rules of the release that wrote it (each log row names that release: harness, the plugin's version and the git commit). Every guarded transition of the machines is marked as one of two kinds, never inferred from its shape: an admission rule ("admission": true), which has no target and no actions and takes the event by doing nothing, so runtime.apply refuses it; or a route ("route": <id>), which changes state or runs actions. A route id is stable: it names the route, is unique across the machines, and does not change when transitions are added, reordered or have their guard's params changed. Admission decides only when an event is sent: the host invariants runtime.apply refuses by (envelope, writerNotOlder, prBinding, agentEvents, oneUnboundSpawn, tapOnly) and the machines' admission rules. Each log row records the route the event took (route: the ids of the routes its transitions took, in every machine, in order; [] when none). Replay (harness replay, harness doctor, the history join) applies each logged event again without any admission: no host refusal and no admission rule for that event (events the machines send each other keep theirs), only its state change. A row with a route takes that route: each route is taken exactly when the row names it, whatever its guard says today; a row whose route cannot be taken again is a divergence. A row written before routes were recorded has none: it takes today's routes when they give the effects the log holds for it (outbox.jsonl), and otherwise the one route that, taken or passed over, gives them, found by search; only such rows are searched. So a rule tightened or loosened later replays an old event as the code that wrote it did, never by a cutoff time. An event's closes (closes) are facts too: replay puts the host's own acks on its scratch copy in time order, so the same effects are pending as when the event was written, and the effects it closes must be exactly the ones the log acks withdrawn by that event; a routed row that closes otherwise, or any row whose log closes an effect replay does not, is a divergence, and a row from before routes were recorded that closes more today than its log does was written by a release that closed less. Replay lists every event today's rules would refuse, route otherwise or close more for (admittedThen) with its id and the release that wrote it (and, for a searched row, that its route was found by its effects): the rules changed since it was written, which is not a problem. An event no route reproduces, a lost event or a rebuilt state that differs is one: the store is corrupt or lost an event.
store.records: A transition marked "record": true takes its event as a fact, in any state of its machine, a final one included: it has no target and no actions, so the event changes no state and queues no effect, and runtime.apply writes its log row. The guards before it in its list still refuse what they refuse when the event is sent; they are admission rules (facts), so replay passes over them and a logged event a record took reaches the record again: no state change, route [] (no route). workItem takes OUT_OF_BAND this way.

eras.description: A store read into a history is an era: its rows were admitted by the rules of their time, and its state.json is the era's own record of where those rules took each item. A history ends a store's era with one ERA_ENDED row after the store's rows (history.schema.json; scripts/history/join.mjs --from writes one per store), carrying the store's harness snapshot as its state.json holds it and the effects its outbox holds that it never acked (pending). Replay (harness replay, harness doctor, the history join) does not apply a row of an era that a later ERA_ENDED row ends: a row its store wrote, or a row recovered from elsewhere (GitHub, a session) addressed to an item the era's snapshot holds and placed before that era's mark. Today's rules do not re-judge it: the era's record holds what it did, and its step names its era. The ERA_ENDED row itself is applied only as a fact (sent, no machine takes it, so runtime.apply refuses it): each child its snapshot holds (its items, and budget) replaces the harness's child of that key, so a later era's record of an item wins; the harness's state value and each of its context fields become the snapshot's, except a field byItem names, a list each of whose elements names an item (the pattern's first group), which keeps its elements for the items the snapshot does not hold and takes the snapshot's for the rest; and the pending effects are queued as the mark's own. Every other row, before a mark or after, is applied by today's machine as a fact (facts). A row is known by its era and its id: ids are unique within a store, not across stores, so two stores' rows with one id are two rows, each a fact of its own era.

pages.description: A page refreshes only when a viewer presses its refresh button: nothing refreshes on a schedule or without a viewer. Each refresh is timed from the press to the rendered page and recorded as one row in the Artifact db collection refreshCollection ({page, at, ms, storeVersion, schemaVersion, bytes, ok}; for a page that reads the history, storeVersion is its row count and schemaVersion its rows' layout, history.schema.json); the page shows the recent rows, and harness doctor --refreshes flags a row slower than refreshSlowMs. A file a page reads beside its own (pages/<page>/needs.json reads.with: flow replay's steps.jsonl, introspection's usage.jsonl) is read again on each refresh with it. A section a page reads on demand (reads.onDemand: the ledger's Time and tokens, usage.jsonl) reads its file only when a viewer opens it, through the same files capability; it is not a refresh, so it is not timed or recorded, and a failed read is said in that section alone.

ORCHESTRATOR_STARTED.description: Refused unless the actor is a session. Its id becomes the orchestrator's, here and in every queued or in-flight item, so no run it reports itself is taken.

AUDIT_PICKED.description: Refused unless a session sends it: the session that read the decision log and picked (harness audit).

Refused unless its day is the UTC day of the event's own time (receivedAt: the at the runtime logs it with, never the sender's word), so a past or future day is refused and there is at most one audit per real day, a day not audited before, and it names 1 to max picks, each a logPrecedent effect id. The picks name decisions only; what each decided is read from the store's own outbox, never from the event.

GRANT_ASKED.description: Refused unless a session sends it: the session the person asked, to put the grant checklist in front of the person. Asking grants nothing: the card's options are the machine's (spec grant), and only the person's tap on it records a grant.

PERSON_GRANTED.description: Refused unless the actor is a person and the source a message: a session, an agent, the lead, a timer or an event with no source cannot grant. A grant from the person's words names the message they are in (message:<cmsg id>); the tap on a checklist goes to its grant actor instead.

Refused unless the message ref is one message id (cmsg_...) and picks is a list, each at most once, of kind:<class> for classes in spec decision meta.classes, one-way, and at most one until:<ISO time> after the event's own time (receivedAt). No until is no end time: the grant lasts until the person replaces it. Picks with no kind end the live grant.

GRANT_GIVEN.description: Sent by a grant actor when the person taps its checklist card; the same event from outside (any event with an actor) is refused. Nothing but the person's tap or message (PERSON_GRANTED) creates, widens or extends a grant.

DECIDED_UNDER_GRANT.description: Sent by a decision the stand-in decided under the person's grant; the same event from outside (any event with an actor) is refused, so no row is written for a decision the grant did not make.

REASK_UNDER_GRANT.description: Refused unless the orchestrator's own session sends it: it routes the work, so it alone re-asks.

Refused unless the decision named is in the person's inbox (waiting on the person) and the harness's live grant covers it at the event's own time (receivedAt): not ended, naming the decision's class, and for a one-way door with the one-way-door box (decision grantCovers). A decision the grant does not cover stays with the person.

REQUEST_RECEIVED.description: Refused when the request has no id, or sets a field the work item's machine holds (tier, criteria, checks, workers, orchestrator, requester and the rest of its context, all but id and project). The filer names the work; triage sets the tier and the criteria. The requester is the event's actor, recorded by the item.

scheduler.description: Holds the WIP limit. WIP_SET from the orchestrator records a new wipLimit (the first one keeps init's as wipLimitAtInit, which replay starts from); outside accepting it starts nothing, and lowering it never stops an item in flight. An item that finishes, even one cancelled while still queued, leaves inFlight and queued, so no slot goes to it; and whenever items start, any id in inFlight or queued whose item has already finished is dropped (a store from before that rule), so a finished item never holds a slot.

BUDGET_MODE.description: Sent by the budget actor when its mode changes inside the harness; the same event from outside (any event with an actor) is refused.

ITEM_PARKED.description: Sent by an item when it enters needsCriteria: it waits on the person and gives up its slot. The same event from outside (any event with an actor) is refused.

WIP_SET.description: Refused unless the orchestrator's own session sends it (the actor is a session whose id is context.orchestrator): any other session, an agent, the person or a tap is refused. The orchestrator routes the work, so it alone sets how much runs at once.
Refused unless limit is an integer from min to max.

accepting.description: Start ready items while fewer than wipLimit are in flight, and again at once when WIP_SET raises the limit.

REQUEST_RECEIVED.description: Refused when the request has no id, or sets a field the work item's machine holds (tier, criteria, checks, workers, orchestrator, requester and the rest of its context, all but id and project). The filer names the work; triage sets the tier and the criteria. The requester is the event's actor, recorded by the item.

ITEM_PARKED.description: Sent by an item when it enters needsCriteria: it waits on the person and gives up its slot. The same event from outside (any event with an actor) is refused.

WIP_SET.description: Refused unless the orchestrator's own session sends it (the actor is a session whose id is context.orchestrator): any other session, an agent, the person or a tap is refused. The orchestrator routes the work, so it alone sets how much runs at once.
Refused unless limit is an integer from min to max.

draining.description: Soft budget limit: nothing new starts; items in flight are told to wrap up.

halted.description: Budget stop: nothing runs until usage allows.

needsPerson.description: The person's inbox is not empty: it holds every open decision and every item waiting in needsCriteria, and each leaves it when it closes (DECISION_CLOSED).
